Yesterday I did the same old mistake.

I was feeling good and work was going great so... I kept going. Big mistake!

1am I was still on it. 2am I was still on it... Then I forced myself to stop. 

I ended up with ~30m latency, slept 6h20m and woke up feeling not well rested
↓
1722582299894554928 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT 
I really need to figure out how to move the way I was feeling by the end of the day into the beginning of the day...

Every day it feels like I am going up the mountain and sometimes by the end I am enjoying a nice view so I want to go higher and higher...
↓
1722582302440448146 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT 
A good night of sleep feels like restarting the day with a higher baseline, but when I am in that place I get a scarcity mindset about that state and I feel like I have to take the max out of it, for it might not come again...
↓
1722582305141653511 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT  [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
So when I go late to bed I think I am trying to reach for this State or trying to maximize the output if I reach it. Sometimes desperately so! Most of the times this is a bad move.
↓
1722582307779887468 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT 
If I go earlier to bad I notice the Sleep Call, usually the closest I take it the better I sleep and feel rested in the morning.

There's kind of a shutting down ritual, which when I am desperately trying to reach The State I reject/neglect.
↓
1722582310887797135 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT 
There's a rhythm to the Sleep Call; a window of opportunity. If one misses it, one pays the price. Sometimes it's a worthy trade-off, but, alas, it is so very rarely!
↓
1722582313978958130 [2023-11-09] @IaimforGOAT 
And so today I wake up feeling yet again in the base of the mountain, where the resolve is lower, the confi-dance is more volatile, the energy is murky, and the day starts off harder than it needed to be.
↓

But also hopeful. Hopeful that there's insights here that I can integrate so I finally fix my sleep. Hopeful that I learn to get into the State without burning bridges. Hopeful that I learn to let it go when letting it go is the better move.

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand centers on the phenomenon of 'revenge bedtime procrastination'—staying up late as a form of magical thinking or control-seeking when the day hasn't gone as planned. The boundary object is @nosilverv's viral 2020 tweet framing it as 'denialist magical thinking.' The arc shows evolution from personal confession (2013-2020) to collective recognition (2020 viral moment) to deeper psychological excavation (2023-2024) exploring embodiment, scarcity mindset, and emotional avoidance. It's primarily dialectical—people validating and refining the shared experience—with some constructive elements (@workflowsauce's somatic solutions). The strand has moderate utility as it names a common problem and generates some tactical wisdom, but lacks a durable artifact or institutional outcome.

title: Staying up late is magical thinking (and we all do it)
summary:
The most brutal line came from @nosilverv: staying up late is “denialist magical thinking” — like you can brute-force a better day by iterating “10 more minutes” until midnight becomes 2am. That tweet (Nov 2020) was the catalyst that turned a private shame-spiral into a named pattern people could quote at themselves.

Once it hit, the thread became a group confession booth. @exgenesis admitted they’re “afraid of going to sleep because the days aren’t running smoothly,” and @natural_hazard sharpened it with the “good counter” metaphor: you stay up until you’ve earned enough “good” to justify ending the day, even though staying up is what guarantees you won’t. Earlier breadcrumbs were already there: @easoncxz (May 2020) wondered if staying up late is a way to sabotage tomorrow so you have “an excuse for failure,” and later reframed the late-night “motivation” that @goblinodds complained about as not motivation at all, but “fear, anxiety, regret, self-blame.”

The discourse peaks when it stops being just willpower talk and becomes mechanics: @IaimforGOAT’s 2023 mini-thread turns it into a scarcity problem (“The State” is rare, so you try to max it out at night), plus a missed “Sleep Call” window that you pay for the next day. By 2024, @workflowsauce pushes it into embodiment: end-of-day feels calm because “it took me all day to stabilize,” and the fix isn’t a harsher bedtime but building “Emotional Self-Intimacy” — keeping 5–15% awareness on bodily check-ins so you’re not fleeing yourself until nighttime finally feels safe. The whole thing kind of “dies” into meme-wisdom by 2025: @blakeaburge’s clean rule, “don’t let your 10pm feelings turn into 7am consequences.”

Why care: it’s not just “stop scrolling.” It’s a map of why bedtime procrastination happens (control, avoidance, scarcity of flow, nervous system settling) and the rare part of Twitter that actually hands you a diagnosis *and* a couple plausible exits.
